system.description:
Summoners are the only class that are born with their gifts, however they still must undergo Stryder training to unlock their true latent abilities. A Summoner can use the Spirit Gates on their bodies to call forth Spirits of the Wild, granting them physical forms and having them battle alongside them. Summoners are well rounded fighters who can flex into martial or magyk prowess while still utilizing their summons at a maximum efficiency.

Level 1 — Blessed Physiology

Your Health starts at 6, and you gain 2 Health every time you gain a level.

The Binding Gates

Summoners possess four gates, each summoning a different spirit with a different effect. You can summon these Spirit Beasts into an unoccupied space within 3 spaces as a 2 Stamina Swift action, or sacrifice a Rank 4 component to ignore paying the Stamina cost. All Spirits' Abilities are Swift Actions which cost you 1 Stamina. The first time a Spirit uses its Primary or Defense Ability it has no Stamina cost. You may only have one Spirit join you in combat at a time. Should you summon a second, the first one is sent through its Gate, exiting combat.

Spirit Beasts use your Resistances when rolling Resistance. Spirit Beasts gain +3 when rolling to Resist [Magykal] abilities.

Crimson Gate — Beast of Destruction
Small size, 7 Health, 7 Movement.
Primary: Make an attack with a range of 1 that deals 5 damage.
Defense: When your Spirit takes damage, make a counter attack dealing 3 damage to the creature that harmed it.

Violet Gate — Beast of Protection
Small size, 10 Health, 7 Movement.
Primary: If the Spirit is within 7 spaces of a creature who is the target of an Attack, it moves to the creatures side and takes the damage instead, then entering the nearest unoccupied space.
Defense: By bracing itself this Spirit takes 3 less damage from the oncoming attack.

Azure Gate — Beast of Freedom
Small size, 4 Health, 10 Flying Speed.
Primary: If the Spirit is within 10 spaces of an ally that must make an Evasion roll, it swoops in and tries to fly them out of the affected area. The ally must still make an Evasion Roll but does not need to use movement.
Primary II: You can evoke Hexes from this Spirits location.
Defense: This Spirit can use Dodge and Evasion. Its Dodge is equal to [1d6 + 4].

Sage Gate — Beast of Solace
Small size, 5 Health, 7 Running Speed.
Ability: The Spirit inflicts the Energized Condition on 1 or 2 creatures within 3 Spaces.
Defence: When it becomes the target of an attack, its attacker becomes Shocked.

Level 4 — Reinforced Gates

The first time you summon any of your Spirit Beasts during a Combat, it gains +4 Health.

Myriad Gates

You can now have up to two Spirit Beasts join you in combat. If a third is summoned, the first one is sent through its Gate, exiting combat.

Sacrificed Remains I

When using Rank 3 components to summon your Spirit Beasts, each type of component grants a unique benefit.

  • Unique: Crimson — Primary ability deals +2 damage
  • Unique: Violet — Defense ability reduces damage by an additional 1
  • Unique: Azure — Gains +1 to Dodge
  • Unique: Sage — Primary ability can Energize up to 3 allies
  • Bones: +2 Speed
  • Sensories: Reduce first instance of damage by half
  • Mana-veins: Unique effect
  • Hearts: +5 Health

Level 8 — Size and Matter

Your Spirit Beasts all become Medium sized.

Mana Exchange

When summoning a Spirit Beast you can do so for a cost of 1 Mana instead of 2 Stamina.

Imbuing Strength

Twice per combat you can reinforce yourself by calling a Spirit Beast back through its gate as a Swift Action. While a Spirit Beast is on the field you may recall it, removing it from combat and granting you a benefit depending on which Spirit Beast was recalled.

  • Crimson: Beast of Destruction — Your next Focused attack deals 10 additional damage.
  • Violet: Beast of Protection — You gain a Ward equal to the Health the Spirit Beast had the moment Imbuing Strength was used.
  • Azure: Beast of Freedom — Your next Leap has double its vertical and horizontal distance, and will deal no falling damage to you.
  • Sage: Beast of Solace — Until the end of the next Player Phase you become Hyper-Energized [Energized with double its benefit].

Sacrificed Remains II

When using Rank 2 or Rank 1 components to summon your Spirit Beasts, each type of component grants a unique benefit.

Rank 2: Unique: Crimson +3 damage | Violet -2 damage | Azure +2 Dodge | Sage Energizes Party regardless of range. Bones: +3 Speed | Sensories: First instance nullified | Mana-veins: Unique | Hearts: +7 Health

Rank 1: Unique: Crimson +5 damage | Violet -4 damage | Azure +3 Dodge | Sage Defense also Stuns. Bones: +4 Speed | Sensories: 1st and 2nd instance nullified | Mana-veins: Unique | Hearts: +10 Health

Level 12 — Chimeric Gate | 1 Stamina, 2 Mana

You can now summon two Spirit Beasts through the same gate causing two Spirits to share one physical form. Choose two Gates to combine and the Spirit Beast that results from your Chimera Gate gains the Health and Speed of both Spirit Beasts as well as an additional 15 Health. Your Chimera can also use both Spirit Beasts abilities. Chimeras count as one Spirit Beast when considering how many are in combat with you. Imbuing Strength can not be used on a Chimera. You can only have one Chimera in combat at a time.

Myriad Gates II

You can now have up to three Spirit Beasts join you in combat. If a third is summoned, the first one is sent through its Gate, exiting combat.

Level 15 — Beast of Disaster | 3 Stamina, 7 Mana

As you reach the apex of your power, you develop the hidden Fifth Gate known as the Golden Divine Gate which summons the Disaster Beast. This beast embodies the natural disasters that can devastate even the grandest of civilizations and return all to the natural world.

You open a massive gate, just enough to drag forth a fraction of this spirits physical form. Choose a 3 space line within range of your summoning, all creatures within those chosen spaces must make an Evasion Roll or take 50 Damage.
